status_policy: Every reviewed proposal keeps status=proposed. This file is a proposed additive patch; it sets no mission_id or task_id and activates nothing. Status may only change when an actual owner, beneficiary and independent reviewer exist.
selection_method: Proposal ids were read from a temporary database seeded by src/civic-engine.js initCivic (44 LDC catalog entries × 17 goals × 4 stages = 2,992 rows, plus 6 Nepal–India tea pilot leads = 2,998). Ids are deterministic, so every listed row exists in any seeded world. No live installation database was read or written.

classification_definitions.duplicate: The question and scope are materially the same as another reviewed proposal (here: an interchangeable stage template reused across countries with no theme-specific criteria). Recommended action: consolidate, do not activate separately.
classification_definitions.useful_proposal: A worthwhile, non-duplicate research question with a real evidence route, but a prior scoping choice or an additional registered source is needed before an owner can scope it.
classification_definitions.missing_evidence: The question is legitimate but the required country or buyer evidence is absent from the registered catalog, so it cannot be answered as written.
classification_definitions.ready_for_human_scoping: Question, scope, outputs, acceptance rubric, source categories, rights and dependencies are concrete enough that a human owner and independent reviewer can scope it now. Nothing is activated.

notes: Keyed by research_leads.id; ids are stable and deterministic.
status is never written by this patch.
proposed_lead_patch.instructions/rubric are proposals, not applied changes; an applying tool must require a named owner, beneficiary and independent reviewer first.
duplicate rows carry no rewrite, only a consolidation recommendation.
